reviews.title: No recurring tasks for free
reviews.text: Not being able to set a task to occur at the same time every day without buying a pro version is genuinely mind boggling to me. That’s the entire point of apps like these, and that feature is easily accessible on many free apps like Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple’s Reminders. I don’t have the energy to reenter every task I want done that day when I am aiming for consistency in my life and generally want the same daily schedule. I came for the pleasing aesthetics but the lack of this feature makes it useless to me

reviews.title: Paid for Lifetime, Disappointed by Missing Two-Way Calendar Sync
reviews.text:
Structured is a great app in many respects, and I paid for the lifetime subscription. However, the lack of two-way calendar sync is a major limitation for me. I need changes made in the app to update my calendar and vice versa.

That’s why I use the lifetime version of Planny, another German app, instead. For a paid planning app, seamless two-way calendar integration is something I consider essential. Disappointing that Structured still doesn’t offer it.

It’s also difficult if you need to make a change in your schedule.

reviews.title: Battery drain and overheating since latest update and macOS 27
reviews.text:
Since the latest Structured update combined with the upgrade to macOS 27, the app has been consuming a massive amount of battery and causing my MacBook Pro Max to run hot even when it is completely closed.
In Activity Monitor the Energy Impact sits at 6,471.1 with a 12 hr Power of 1,035.90. App Nap is off. It keeps running in the background and draining the battery continuously. This is new behavior after the recent updates.
Please fix the background activity and extreme energy use as soon as possible

reviews.title: Important features missing
reviews.text:
I thought I had finally found my perfect task management app, but sadly not.  

Unfortunately there is no facility to allocate a priority to tasks.  A key part of time management is capturing the tasks that need doing and being able to prioritise them BEFORE you schedule them in your day.  This app jumps straight into scheduling without giving a system for choosing which tasks are actually needed.   In an ideal world you should be able to set up a system for how you prioritise your tasks (there are a variety of different ways), and view your tasks in a priority view THEN schedule. Apps like tick tick or todoist do this very well but don’t have the visual appeal of Structured.  I would totally switch if the task capturing and prioritisation side of Structured was improved.

reviews.title: I wish I bought the lifetime membership when the app was new
reviews.text: I remember using this app a ton while in high school and loving it and after being out of it for a bit I felt like I needed to plan my days better rather than just trying to keep a vague idea of how long I’m going to set time aside for things in my head. So I remembered I used this app so I redownloaded it and immediately felt depressed with it. So much of the features I need are locked behind a payment that’s too expensive for me right now and I can’t just remake my schedule by hand every day like I used to when I was in high school and the app was new because I just don’t have the time or energy to do that anymore. I wanted to get the lifetime membership when the app was really new and only like $5 or something but my parents said it wasn’t worth it and wouldn’t let me get it. Is there a way to get it for that price again or is it just too late? This app is perfect for what I need right now to plan my day and other day planners in the AppStore don’t feel right but if I have to either deal with that huge price or huge inefficiency with the free version I’ll have to find another app.
